phish.name: Phishing and fraud
phish.rec: Pause when you feel urgency. Check the sender and the real link, and verify through an official channel you open yourself.

pass.name: Passwords, MFA and privacy
pass.rec: Use a long unique passphrase for each important account, turn on MFA, and never share OTPs.

foot.name: Digital footprint
foot.rec: Review what your profiles reveal about where you live, travel and spend your time, and tighten audiences and location tags.

mis.name: Misinformation
mis.rec: Before sharing, find the original source, check the date, look for independent confirmation and verify images.

tech.name: Responsible technology use
tech.rec: Follow your institution's rules, respect other people's privacy and verify AI-generated output.

questions.q: You get an SMS: “Your bank account is restricted. Tap the link to restore access.” What is the best first step?
o: Tap the link quickly before the account closes
Reply with your details so they can help
Ignore the link and check using the bank's official app or number
Forward it to friends to check
questions.e: Never use links in unexpected alerts. Contact the bank through channels you already trust.

questions.q: Which is the strongest sign of advance-fee fraud?
o: The message has a deadline
You must pay a fee before receiving a prize or scholarship
It mentions your university
It has a friendly tone
questions.e: Paying upfront to unlock a reward is the hallmark of advance-fee fraud.

questions.q: An email from “university support” comes from a free Gmail address and asks you to verify your login within 24 hours. What should you do?
o: Verify quickly in case it is real
Reply asking for proof
Forward it to your class group
Open the official portal by typing its address, or contact the ICT office
questions.e: Independent verification through official channels is safest. The sender address and urgency are warning signs.

questions.q: Which approach to passwords is best?
o: One strong password for every account
A long unique passphrase for each important account, kept in a password manager
Your birthday with a symbol
Sharing passwords with a trusted friend
questions.e: Unique passphrases limit the damage if one account is breached. Password managers make this practical.

o: A second proof of identity beyond your password
A faster login
Protection only for banks
Nothing if your password is strong
questions.e: MFA means a stolen password alone is not enough. Never share the codes you receive.

questions.q: Which public post carries the most risk?
o: A photo from a coding club meeting
A favourite song
“Travelling Friday. My hostel, Block C Room 14, will be empty for two weeks.”
Congratulating a friend
questions.e: It shows where you live and when it will be empty. Share trips after you return.

questions.q: You post something embarrassing and delete it quickly. What is true?
o: It is gone forever
Others may already have copied or screenshotted it
Only friends could see it
Deleting always removes backups
questions.e: Deleting helps but cannot guarantee removal. Think before posting.

questions.q: A viral message says exams are cancelled, with no source. What is the best first step?
o: Share it so others know
Believe it if many people forward it
Check official channels and the original source before sharing
Delete it and ignore it for good
questions.e: Popularity is not proof. Verify with official sources first.

questions.q: A dramatic photo is shared with the caption “happening now”. How can you check it?
o: Count the likes
Run a reverse image search and look at the date and original source
Trust it if the caption is detailed
Ask the poster to swear it is real
questions.e: Old images are often reused with new captions. Check where and when it first appeared.

questions.q: Which is an example of responsible technology use?
o: Posting a coursemate's photo without asking
Using a friend's login for convenience
Downloading cracked software
Using AI tools as your institution allows, verifying outputs and crediting help where required
questions.e: Responsible use respects rules, privacy and honesty.
